newsitem.title: UK: BP, Mobil see higher joint venture savings.
newsitem.headline: BP, Mobil see higher joint venture savings.

text.p: British Petroleum Plc and Mobil Corp. said Friday they expected savings from their European refining and marketing joint venture to exceed the $400 million to $500 million estimated in February.

The joint venture, announced on Feb. 29, will combine about $5 billion worth of the companies' refining and marketing assets in Europe. BP and Mobil said at the time that the annual cost savings would be between $400 million and $500 million before taxes.

In a joint statement, BP and Mobil said they were "delighted with the progress on the joint venture," which was proceeding on schedule on a country-by-country basis and was likely to be completed during the second quarter of next year.

The companies also said they expected to reap more than $200 million in proceeds by streamlining marketing assets and selling surplus offices and that one-time costs of $740 million before tax would exceed original estimates.

BP would take exceptional charges before tax of around $490 million and $40 million in fees, expenses and write-downs in the fourth quarter. After tax, the charge would amount to around $430 million, the companies said.

Mobil's costs for restructuring would be around $330 million before tax, resulting in an after-tax charge of around $145 million in the fourth quarter. In addition, Mobil would incur one-time after-tax special charges in 1997 and 1998 of around $110 million.
